title: Behold, the Grace Appears
description: Behold, the Grace Appears in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 3, headed “The nativity of Christ, Luke 1. 30 &c. Luke 2, 10 &c”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold, the grace ap-pears, The pro-mise is ful-fill'd; Ma-ry the won-drous vir-gin bears, And Je-sus is the child.

lines: He bids him rule the lands abroad,
The nations shall his grace obtain,
He tells the shepherds of their joys,
And straight, a flaming troop was seen;
With the celestial host we join,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
